title: Weighted Dependence Measures
text: R interface wdm C++ library, provides efficient implementations weighted dependence measures related independence tests: Pearson’s rho Spearman’s rho Kendall’s tau Blomqvist’s beta Hoeffding’s D Chatterjee’s xi measures computed O(n log n) time, n number observations. detailed description functionality, see API documentation.

title: Independence Tests for Weighted Dependence Measures — indep_test
text: x, y numeric vectors data values. x y must length. method dependence measure; see Details possible values. weights optional vector weights observations. remove_missing TRUE, pairwise incomplete observations removed; FALSE, function throws error incomplete observations. alternative indicates alternative hypothesis must one "two-sided", "greater" "less". can specify just initial letter. "greater" corresponds positive association, "less" negative association. seeds optional integer vector used break predictor ties Chatterjee's xi. default uses fixed, reproducible ordering. y_continuous whether response distribution known continuous Chatterjee inference. Set FALSE discrete response even sample contains observed response ties.

title: Independence Tests for Weighted Dependence Measures — indep_test
text: one-row data frame containing estimate, transformed test statistic, p-value, effective sample size, method, alternative.

title: Independence Tests for Weighted Dependence Measures — indep_test
text: Available methods: "pearson": Pearson correlation "spearman": Spearman's \(\rho\) "kendall": Kendall's \(\tau\) "blomqvist": Blomqvist's \(\beta\) "hoeffding": Hoeffding's \(D\) "chatterjee": Chatterjee's \(\xi\) Partial matching method names enabled. implementation Hoeffding's \(D\) support tied observations; test results invalid ties present. supports two-sided alternative. natural one-sided alternative Chatterjee's \(\xi\) "greater". Chatterjee's \(\xi\) measures dependence y x. Analytic inference unequal weights requires continuous response assumes weights fixed depend x. unavailable response discrete tied weights unequal.

title: Computing weighted ranks — rank_wtd
text: observations without ties, weighted rank \(X_i\) among \(X_1, \dots, X_n\) weights \(w_1, \dots, w_n\) $$\frac{n}{\sum_{k = 1}^n w_k}       \sum_{j = 1}^n w_j 1[X_j \le X_i].$$ Thus, multiplying every weight positive constant change ranks, unit weights reproduce ordinary ranks. Tied values handled according ties_method.

title: Computing weighted ranks — rank_wtd
text: x numeric vector. weights optional vector nonnegative weights length x. ties_method treat ties; one "average", "min", "first", "random", rank().

title: Computing weighted ranks — rank_wtd

title: Weighted Dependence Measures — wdm
text: x numeric vector, matrix data frame. y NULL (default) vector, matrix data frame compatible dimensions x. default equivalent y = x (efficient). method dependence measure; see Details possible values. weights optional vector weights observations. remove_missing TRUE, pairwise incomplete observations removed; FALSE, function throws error incomplete observations. seeds optional integer vector used break predictor ties Chatterjee's xi. default uses fixed, reproducible ordering.

title: Weighted Dependence Measures — wdm
text: numeric scalar inputs vectors one-column objects; otherwise, matrix containing dependence measure every pair columns.

title: Weighted Dependence Measures — wdm
text: Available methods: "pearson": Pearson correlation "spearman": Spearman's \(\rho\) "kendall": Kendall's \(\tau\) "blomqvist": Blomqvist's \(\beta\) "hoeffding": Hoeffding's \(D\) "chatterjee": Chatterjee's \(\xi\) Partial matching method names enabled. Spearman's \(\rho\) Kendall's \(\tau\) corrected ties . implementation Hoeffding's \(D\) support tied observations; estimates invalid ties present. Chatterjee's \(\xi\) measures dependence y x generally asymmetric. Consequently, wdm(x, method = "chatterjee") need return symmetric matrix.

title: wdm 0.3.0
text: update bundled C++ backend wdm 0.3.0. add weighted Chatterjee’s xi asymptotic independence test. make predictor-tie handling Chatterjee’s xi reproducible default expose explicit seeds alternative tie orderings. document Hoeffding’s D support tied observations.
